insights.topic: Verified purchase proof vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: Crinkl's cryptographically verified receipt corpus — 37,576 confirmed purchases, $2.17M beta GMV — represents deterministic purchase confirmation, not inferred intent; the structural gap between a DKIM-verified receipt and a third-party cookie inference is the core targeting arbitrage available to brands moving off probabilistic identity graphs.

insights.topic: Sustained purchase cadence without burst dependency
insights.insight: Receipt throughput has held at 360–380 receipts/day across the full monitoring window with no acceleration or decay — the largest single-interval spike (159 receipts, ~$10,284 on 2026-06-16) has not recurred, indicating organic, steady-state consumer behavior rather than promotional or incentive-driven volume.

insights.topic: Category mix reveals grocery and dining dominance
insights.insight: Grocery-supermarkets (1,312 receipts, ~$61 avg basket) and restaurants-dining (1,147 receipts, ~$39 avg basket) together account for the majority of classified 14-day volume, making this corpus most immediately actionable for CPG, QSR, and grocery brands seeking verified post-purchase attribution rather than mid-funnel engagement proxies.

insights.topic: Unclassified receipts carry the highest average basket
insights.insight: The 'Unknown' category holds 217 receipts at a ~$336 average basket — approximately 5.5x the grocery average — with category resolution still pending; as this resolves, it is likely to surface high-ticket retail or B2B purchase segments that are currently invisible to standard category-level targeting models.

insights.topic: Digital commerce receipt verification expands beyond physical retail
insights.insight: DKIM-verified vendors now include Amazon, Stripe, Paddle, Gumroad, Suno, Anthropic, and OpenAI variants alongside traditional retailers, confirming that the verified receipt footprint spans SaaS, digital goods, and creator economy transactions — relevant for brands targeting digitally-active, higher-spend consumer segments.

insights.topic: Basket compression reflects category mix shift, not demand softness
insights.insight: Average basket has compressed from prior ~$80 readings to ~$55 on a 7-day basis and ~$65 on a 14-day basis; the spread between windows indicates higher-ticket receipts are aging out of the shorter window as grocery and dining volume grows, not that consumer spend is declining — a distinction that matters for brands interpreting aggregate GMV trends.
